Wintermute Warns Crypto Bear Market Isn't Over, Recent Selloff No Sign of a Bottom Crypto market maker Wintermute warned in its November 16 market report that the bear market is far from over, with Bitcoin falling 12.7% last week to around $65,400, below its 200-week moving average near $68,000. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $1.9 billion in net outflows so far in 2026, compared with $21 billion in inflows in 2025, while stablecoin supply has shrunk by $14 billion to $16 billion over the past 30 days. Wintermute said recent liquidations do not signal a market bottom, as rebounds appear driven by short covering rather than fresh capital. The firm warned Bitcoin could fall into the $50,000s and would reconsider its defensive stance only if BTC reclaimed $68,000 alongside renewed ETF inflows. — link

Trezor Says Shipping Partner Data Breach Exposed 27,000 Customer Orders Trezor, a leading cryptocurrency hardware wallet manufacturer, disclosed that a breach at shipping partner Skladon exposed personal information linked to approximately 27,000 orders placed between August 9 and November 7. Skladon notified Trezor on November 15 that attackers had accessed its systems and were believed to have exported customer names, phone numbers, addresses, emails and order details. The breach affected multiple countries but not U.S. customers. Trezor said its own systems and hardware wallets remained secure, warning users of phishing scams and potential physical security risks. https://x.com/Trezor/status/2122363569891135655?a=VEd-7HQE5FC-nrMNBqk&s=20 — link

Ex-Robinhood Engineer Faces Up to 20 Years in Prison for Trading Ahead of Crypto Listings The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York announced that former Robinhood software engineer Huaisong Xiang pleaded guilty to wire fraud for using confidential crypto listing information to trade perpetual futures on Hyperliquid. Between 2025 and 2026, Xiang repeatedly traded tokens ahead of their listing announcements on Robinhood Crypto, the digital asset trading arm of the U.S. brokerage, earning $125,523 in illicit profits. He agreed to forfeit the proceeds and faces up to 20 years in prison, with sentencing scheduled for February 25, 2027. — link

Italy's Largest Bank Cuts ARK Bitcoin ETF Stake 43%, BlackRock Ether Staking ETF 57% Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's largest banking group, significantly reshuffled its crypto ETF holdings in Q3 2026, according to Criptovaluta's analysis of U.S. regulatory filings. The bank cut its ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF stake by 42.9% to 1.98 million shares and reduced its BlackRock Ethereum staking ETF holdings by 56.6%. Meanwhile, its Bitwise Solana Staking ETF position grew to 875,407 shares worth $14.14 million, while it added $6.7 million in Bitwise XRP ETF shares and $599,000 in Bitwise Hyperliquid ETF holdings. — link
